item.title: Glenohumeral Traction
patientPosition: Supine with shoulder in resting position, often slight abduction/flexion as comfortable.
therapistPosition: Stand beside shoulder with arm supported.
contact: Grasp proximal humerus close to joint line using both hands or belt-assisted technique.
forceDirection: Traction perpendicular to glenoid treatment plane.
Grade I neutralizes compression, Grade II takes up slack, Grade III stretches capsule.
dosage: Sustained holds commonly 10–30 seconds repeated 3–5 times, adjusted to response.
steps: 4. Progress to Grade III only in stiffness-dominant presentation.
mistakes: Pulling distal arm instead of creating joint distraction.
Using Grade III in high irritability.
safety: Avoid acute dislocation, fracture, unstable repair.
item.visualCue: Scapula fixed → Humeral head distracted from glenoid → Re-test ROM.

subTechniques.name: Glenohumeral Grade I–III Traction
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Use Grade I to reduce compression, Grade II to take up slack and Grade III to stretch a restricted capsule when irritability permits.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the shoulder near its resting position and the arm supported.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize the scapula and grasp the proximal humerus close to the joint line; a belt may be used by a trained clinician.
subTechniques.direction: Apply traction perpendicular to the glenoid treatment plane. The grade is defined by slack/tissue resistance, not by arbitrary force.
subTechniques.dosage: 10–30 second sustained holds repeated 3–5 times with reassessment.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: The treatment plane determines the direction. Pulling on the distal arm without controlling the joint is not precise traction.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid acute dislocation, fracture or unstable repair.

subTechniques.name: Posterior Translatoric Glide
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve selected flexion/internal-rotation restriction when posterior translatoric glide is indicated.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the scapula stabilized and humerus supported near the treatment position.
subTechniques.contact: Broad contact over the anterior proximal humerus close to the joint.
subTechniques.direction: Glide the humeral head posteriorly parallel to the treatment plane after appropriate traction/slack is taken up.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Kaltenborn glides are sustained translatoric movements—not rhythmic Maitland oscillations.
